title: Gas Trader I, II, III or  IV
description:
We are looking for talented individuals who are passionate about making an impact in the company and the community. Apply now and become part of the dynamic energy industry!

Position Description:

Responsible for ensuring reliable and cost-effective natural gas supply to meet the forecasted demand of Tucson Electric Power, UNS Electric, and UNS Gas. Collaborates on daily gas trading activities to optimize the company’s portfolio of transportation and storage assets, incorporating forward-looking volume forecasts and price signals to support informed decision-making.
Identifies and executes opportunities to monetize excess natural gas, pipeline capacity, and storage positions through structured transactions and market-based strategies, ensuring compliance with contractual and regulatory requirements while maximizing asset value. Evaluates existing transportation agreements and large wholesale gas customer demand to maintain sufficient system capacity, optimize portfolio and long-term contract performance.
Develops and maintains strong working relationships with natural gas suppliers, pipeline operators, and other key counterparties to support reliable operations and market access. Synthesizes market intelligence (forward curves, basis spreads, pipeline constraints, volumes and regional fundamentals) into actionable trading and commercial strategies.
Develops, implements, and continuously enhances trading strategies aligned with the companies’ participation in current and evolving wholesale markets, ensuring operational reliability, cost efficiency, and strategic positioning.

Key Responsibilities:

Gas Trader I

- Executes physical gas trades across day-ahead and real-time markets for TEP, UNS Electric, and UNS Gas to optimize transportation and portfolio value under the guidance of senior personnel.

- Daily activities include load and resource forecasting, deal execution, pipeline nominations, and required deal documentation.

- Available during standard & non-standard business hours including weekends as needed to support pipeline Operational Flow Orders (OFOs) and provide real-time updates on actual gas availability. Monitors and manages gas nominations, gas schedules, imbalances and system conditions and assists Real-Time Energy Traders, as needed.

- Overseeing nominations, confirmations, and curtailments across natural gas pipelines, actively trading to minimize gas imbalance impacts. Advises the Wholesale Marketing team on emerging issues, operational risks, and market-based solutions.

- Actively reviews the efficiency of the daily gas nominations and accounting reconciliation activities to ensure that those functions are completed in an optimal manner.

- Communicates between suppliers and customers to ensure that contractual nomination data is coordinated accurately throughout the delivery chain.

- Ensures all purchases and sales of natural gas are fully documented and summarized for accounting and billing purposes. Assists back office with invoice reconciliation.

- Performs other functions, job duties, and other Wholesale duties as defined by Supervisor.

Gas Trader II

- Collects market data and assists other traders with market forecasting and analysis. Provides Day Ahead power trading with current expected unit costs.

- Maintains an awareness and understanding of applicable Federal/State regulations and ensures Risk Management procedures and protocols are followed.

- Monitors electronic bulletin boards and collaborates with pipeline company contacts to track key volume activity and implement corrective actions as needed.

- Analyzes load studies, customer usage patterns, and demand forecasts to identify actionable trading and sales opportunities.

- Recommends and executes asset optimization opportunities within established risk management parameters.

- Monitors portfolio exposures and escalates trading, operational, and market risks as appropriate.

Gas Trader III

- Independently executes physical and financial trading strategies that optimize portfolio value and support long-term supply objectives.

- Evaluates trading risks and opportunities within approved risk management frameworks.

- Apply market analytics and historical pricing trends to identify and execute value-enhancing trading opportunities.

- Manages large volume customer contracts.

- Translates market and load insights into structured transactions, NSP offerings, and portfolio optimization strategies.

Gas Trader IV

- Provides strategic recommendations regarding portfolio risk, hedging structures, and market positioning.

- Mentors and develop junior traders. Serves as subject matter expert for gas markets and transportation strategy.

- Reviews, develops, and implements new natural gas procedures in conjunction with changes in participating market rules or policies.

- Monitors interstate pipeline tariffs and rate cases as required.

- Tracks policy and regulatory changes at applicable markets, the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission and the Arizona Corporation Commission.

- Critically assesses hedging strategies incorporating financial instruments, basis differentials, and optionality.

- Proactively identifies inefficiencies and opportunities for margin enhancement across the gas portfolio.

Minimum Qualifications - Gas Trader I:

- Completion of two years towards a college degree in Engineering, Economics, Business, Finance, or Accounting, or 2 years relevant experience in the utility industry.

- Must have demonstrated electric utility business knowledge and experience.

- Must have strong quantitative, analytical, and computer skills.

- Exceptional time management skills, including ability to prioritize, set, and meet deadlines.

- Working knowledge of the technical principles of electrical generation, natural gas and transmission systems.

- Position requires the ability to work independently, communicate effectively, with emphasis on accuracy and attention to detail.

Preferred Qualifications:

- Electric Utility Industry Knowledge.

- Analytical and Quantitative Skills.

- Understanding of Energy Markets.

- Strong Communication.

​Minimum Qualifications - Gas Trader II:

- College degree in Engineering, Economics, Business, Finance, or Accounting, or 3 years’ relevant experience in the utility industry.

- Ability to procure gas and schedule for multiple affiliates with guidance from senior personnel.

- Working knowledge of Northern American Energy Standards Board (NAESB) contract and International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) Master Agreement.

Preferred Qualifications:

- 2 – 3 years wholesale gas or power trading experience or relevant utility industry experience.

- Knowledge of NAESB and ISDA contracts.

- Broad understanding of the utility business including the effects of decisions on the regulatory process.

Minimum Qualifications – Gas Trader III:

- College degree in Engineering, Economics, Business, Finance, or Accounting, with 5 years’ relevant experience in the utility industry.

- Ability to procure and schedule gas for all affiliates with limited to no guidance from senior personnel.

- Independently develops and executes trading, hedging, and commercial strategies, including NSP transactions and portfolio optimization initiatives.

Preferred Qualifications:

- 4 – 5 years wholesale gas or power trading experience or combination of either. Along with gas or power scheduling experience.

Minimum Qualifications - Gas Trader IV

- 7+ years of natural gas trading or combination of natural gas and power trading experience.

- Must have advanced knowledge of economic and technical principles of the North American natural gas markets and applicable pipeline transportation systems.

- Advanced knowledge and understanding of complex energy and natural gas contracts.

- Strong understanding of futures markets, basis markets, and financial hedging instruments.

Preferred Qualifications:

- 4 years of gas trading with 3 years of relevant trading or equivalent electric utility industry experience.

- Proficient in all aspects of Natural Gas Trading, fundamental and structural, and  quantitative and pricing modeling.

- Ability to create analysis of future demand for core customers.

- Experience in trading both Natural gas and Power.

ADA Requirements and Physical Demands:
The physical demands as described are representative of those that must be met by the person in this position to successfully perform the essential functions of the job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

- Office Work:
- Sit, Stand, Walk and Bend: This position regularly requires prolonged periods of sitting. Occasionally requires standing, walking, or bending for short periods of time.

- Use of Hands/Fingers: To operate a computer, keyboard, mouse, and other office equipment.

- Speech/Hearing: This position frequently communicates with others via phone and in-person.

- Visual Acuity: For reviewing detailed operational reports.

- Lifting: Ability to lift and carry items weighing up to 15 pounds, as needed.

- Safety Sensitive: This position does not perform safety sensitive functions.

- Travel: Regular travel to operational sites, industry events, and stakeholder meetings.

title: Supervisor, GIS Infrastructure IT Applications
description:
We are looking for talented individuals who are passionate about making an impact in the company and the community. Apply now and become part of the dynamic energy industry!

This role leads one of the most significant geospatial transformations in the organization—guiding the enterprise migration to the ArcGIS Utility Network and shaping how GIS supports electric operations for years to come.

You will supervise and support a dedicated and experienced technology team while contributing directly to the evolution of our geospatial systems. In this role, you will work collaboratively with IT partners, operations, field services, and business stakeholders to support the implementation of the ArcGIS Utility Network. You’ll help ensure systems and data support day‑to‑day workflows, maintain reliability and accuracy, and align with long‑term asset management goals. This role is well‑suited for someone who enjoys balancing people leadership with hands‑on technical involvement in a collaborative, forward‑thinking environment.

What You Bring

- Experience supervising or leading GIS, application support, or technical teams in a collaborative, team‑focused environment

- A strong working knowledge of GIS technologies, with interest in learning and supporting modern platforms such as the ArcGIS Utility Network

- The ability to partner effectively with IT, operations, and field teams to understand needs and support practical solutions

- Clear communication skills and a supportive leadership style that helps teams stay aligned and successful

- A problem‑solving mindset and willingness to learn, adapt, and grow alongside evolving technologies

Position Description
Directs, coordinates and administers assigned personnel designated to provide ongoing services and products used by Transmission & Distribution (Geographic Information System – Smallworld Preferred, Outage Management System, Work Management System, Maintenance Management System and other related technologies).  Provides ongoing leadership to ensure services and products required by clients are well understood and tactical direction is set to ensure their delivery.

Position-Related Responsibilities

- Reports to and coordinates closely with the appropriate Director or Supervisor of Information Services to plan and manage the responsibilities of the group.

- Coordinates with clients to ensure a thorough understanding of services and products required.  Adept at understanding the needs of clients from a business perspective.

- Oversees, directs, and coordinates the work of staff members assigned to the group to ensure the delivery of results that meet client needs, and provide for the efficient long term operation of IS.

- Works with other IS groups to ensure the understanding and coordination of effective results.

- Develops and manages budgets which support the cost-effective implementation of strategies, tactics and operating plans within the immediate area of responsibility.

- Provides or ensures effective project leadership for assignments and initiatives the immediate group is involved in.

- Ensures that IS Standards and practices are understood and consistently applied.

- Maintains an effective level of expertise and understanding needed to direct and coordinate those areas of responsibility to ensure success.

- Is responsible for the design, development, and maintenance of the Geographic Information System, Outage Management System, Work Management System, Maintenance Management System and other related technologies supported by the immediate group.

- This position may provide services to affiliates of the Company subject to the UNS Energy Code of Conduct and the related Policies and Procedures.

-

Management Responsibilities

- Ensure that the Company’s management principles, policies and programs are consistently practiced and continually support the Affirmative Action Plan.

- Assume fiduciary responsibility for operating the business and provide recommendations on cost improvement measures.

- Ensure that the Performance Management program is administered uniformly and effectively.

- Comply with and administer the terms and conditions of the Collective Bargaining Agreement when applicable.

- Administers personnel functions, including recruiting, review and approval of job descriptions and salary classifications, and selection and placement of personnel.  Participates in hiring, termination, promoting, assignment and direction of staff.

- Ensure compliance with all applicable local, state and federal laws, regulations and standards, company policies, practices and ethical obligations to investigate, evaluate and recommend appropriate resolution to employee complaints.

- Promotes and participates in the professional development, personal growth and career planning of staff.  Motivate, recognize and reward, coach, counsel, train; provide feedback to employees during performance reviews.   Participates in Leadership Development programs.

- Addresses disciplinary and/or performance issues, according to company policy, and communicates effectively with employees regarding corrective action. Has input into the adjustment of grievances and administration of discipline.

- Plans day-to-day operations, estimates personnel needs and schedules and assigns work.  Evaluate the structure and team plan for continual improvement of the efficiency and effectiveness of the group.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities   (Equivalent combination of education and experience will be considered.)

Minimum Qualifications

- High school diploma or GED.

- Minimum 5 years of experience in the Information Service field and demonstrated experience leading an application support or large project team. Broad knowledge of related application systems and interfaces.

- Strong leadership and inter personal skills required to lead IS staff members and maintain effective relations with clients.

- Experience in the following is required:

- GIS systems

- Business areas of Electric Utilities (experience specifically in Electric Distribution is a plus).

- Analysis for support and problem resolution of GIS systems for utilities.

- Requirements analysis.

- Familiarity with MS Project, PowerPoint, Visio, Word, Excel.

Preferred Qualifications

- Bachelor’s degree in Management Information Systems, Computer Science or related discipline preferred.

- A broad general knowledge of information systems technology subjects, extensive knowledge of hardware and software, and the ability to keep abreast of new technologies.

- Strong business knowledge and experience within the area of responsibility.

- Communicate effectively with clients, direct reports, and management.
